title: Cover the real WebSocket opening handshake without bind()
description: tests/test_mcp_stdio.py::test_websocket_bridge_lists_and_calls_tools_prompts_and_resources and ::test_websocket_bridge_handles_jsonrpc_initialize both call _free_port(), which does socket.bind(('127.0.0.1', 0)). Sandboxed environments (including the one pyacp-0f6 was validated in) deny bind() for AF_INET and AF_UNIX alike, so those two tests fail with PermissionError before exercising any project code. That is 2 of 20 tests -- and specifically the only two that cover the real opening handshake and framing -- silently unavailable wherever an agent or CI runner is network-restricted.
design: Both tests can run without binding anything: pair socket.socketpair() with loop.connect_accepted_socket() for the server side and websockets.connect(uri, sock=...) for the client side. The server needs a WebSocketServer whose wrap() target stubs .sockets, .get_loop(), and .is_serving(). A working proof of this ran all of both tests' assertions unchanged on 3.11/3.12/3.13/3.14 during pyacp-0f6. Options: (a) replace _free_port() with a socketpair fixture outright, (b) keep the TCP path and add a socketpair fallback when bind() raises PermissionError. Prefer (a) -- one transport path, no environment-dependent branching, and nothing about these tests actually needs a TCP port.
acceptance_criteria: Both tests pass in an environment where socket.bind() raises PermissionError; they still assert the same responses they do today; make lint && make test green on every version in the ci.yml matrix; if the harness moves to a shared fixture, tests/ gains no dependency the dev extra does not already provide.
notes:
pyacp-tzd.3 removed the PermissionError half of this bead. The two tests it names no
longer exist: tests/test_transport_ws.py replaced them with socket-free equivalents that
drive a FakeWebSocket through serve_websocket(), and the whole suite (178 tests) now
passes in a sandbox that denies bind().

What is LEFT is the coverage gap this bead's DESIGN already solves. Nothing now exercises
websockets.asyncio.server.serve(), the real opening handshake, or real frame
transmission -- FakeWebSocket bypasses all three. Untested surface is
WebSocketAgentServer.start()/stop()/serve_forever(); _handle_client is covered by
test_the_server_binds_each_accepted_socket_to_an_agent.

The DESIGN's option (a) still applies verbatim: socket.socketpair() +
loop.connect_accepted_socket() for the server, websockets.connect(uri, sock=...) for the
client, needing a stub with .sockets/.get_loop()/.is_serving(). Note the server API moved
from websockets.serve to websockets.asyncio.server.serve, so the wrap() target is now a
ServerConnection rather than a WebSocketServerProtocol.

title: PytestUnraisableExceptionWarning from a subprocess transport on Python 3.11 only
description:
Running the suite on 3.11 emits one warning that 3.14 does not:

  tests/test_transport_stdio.py::test_a_session_can_bring_its_own_mcp_server
  PytestUnraisableExceptionWarning: Exception ignored in:
  <function BaseSubprocessTransport.__del__>
  ... asyncio/base_subprocess.py line 126, in __del__ -> self.close()

The suite passes; this is cleanup noise from an asyncio subprocess transport being
garbage-collected after its loop is gone. It is version-specific (3.11 present, 3.14
absent), so it is most likely a CPython asyncio change rather than anything this repo
does wrong -- but the test does spawn an MCP server subprocess for a session and may
not be tearing it down before the loop closes.

Found while running the ci.yml matrix locally for pyacp-22w. Not caused by that work:
it reproduces on 3.11 with or without those changes.

Worth either fixing the teardown so the transport is closed explicitly, or -- if it is
genuinely a CPython artefact -- adding a targeted filterwarnings with a comment naming
the version, so a NEW unraisable exception is not hidden by a blanket ignore.
acceptance_criteria: Either the 3.11 leg is warning-free, or the warning is suppressed by a narrowly-scoped filter that names the interpreter version and the reason, and a new unraisable exception in another test would still surface.
notes:
Confirmed in GitHub Actions on the 3.11 leg (CPython 3.11.16, ubuntu runner), not just locally — so it is not a macOS or a local-venv artefact.

Note it is NOT a single test. Locally it surfaced on
  tests/test_transport_stdio.py::test_a_session_can_bring_its_own_mcp_server
and in CI on
  tests/test_terminals.py::test_close_all_releases_every_session
Same traceback both times: BaseSubprocessTransport.__del__ -> close() -> call_soon() ->
RuntimeError('Event loop is closed'). It attaches to whichever test happens to be running
when the GC collects a subprocess transport whose loop has already closed, which means a
filterwarnings scoped to one test id would be wrong AND fragile.

That points at the real cause: some test spawns an asyncio subprocess and lets the
transport outlive its event loop instead of closing it. Fixing the teardown is preferable
to suppressing; the suppression fallback should be a global filter naming 3.11 and this
RuntimeError text specifically, so an unrelated unraisable exception still surfaces.

Only 3.11 and 3.14 checked locally (3.12/3.13 not installed on the dev machine); the CI
matrix covers all four and only 3.11 warns.
